title: Real-estate investor: business-public contact route and private-owner hold
hypothesis: The live NC 3–8 parcel investor route cannot currently start because it lacks a register-source mapping. Even if it could, grouping private parcel owners is not a permitted basis for uncovering or appending personal contacts. A permitted future route must begin with an explicitly business-public investor/operator contact and keep owner and handset confirmation separate.
ownerSource: No implemented owner-confirming source is available for this industry. The live brain describes NC parcel-owner grouping as an investor candidate signal only; it does not establish a current business owner, a business purpose for a private contact, or ownership of a handset.
phoneSource: No implemented phone source. A business-public alternative may use an explicitly published business contact from an authorized commercial STR/operator or business-license endpoint, but never a residential parcel record, owner mailing address, or private append.

workflow.label: Start with a business-public endpoint
workflow.detail: Use only an authorized public endpoint that explicitly publishes an operator or business contact for business use. The current parcel-owner grouping is held out of contact discovery.

workflow.label: Business-purpose and role filter
workflow.detail: Require an active commercial/operator or clearly business-facing role, plus a documented permitted-use basis. A parcel owner, landlord, resident, owner mailing address, or title alone fails this filter.

workflow.label: Hold private or ambiguous identity
workflow.detail: Do not create a contact candidate from residential/property data or use it to find a private cell number.

workflow.label: Published business contact present?
workflow.detail: Retain only a contact explicitly published by the business-public source. A named role does not supply a telephone number.

workflow.label: Hold without business-public contact
workflow.detail: Keep no phone candidate and do not append, trace, or reverse-lookup a person from parcel or owner data.

workflow.label: Contact and compliance gates
workflow.detail: Require existing mobile classification, reachability, DNC/TCPA clearance, suppression, duplicate, and freshness gates. Passing these gates does not prove the business owner or handset owner.

workflow.label: Hold failed contact gate
workflow.detail: Hold non-mobile, unreachable, DNC/TCPA, suppressed, duplicate, stale, or otherwise unverified contacts.

workflow.label: Independent ownership and handset evidence?
workflow.detail: A commercial license holder, property-owner name, entity member, published business line, or mobile result alone is candidate evidence only.

workflow.label: Hold as business contact candidate
workflow.detail: Do not label or deliver an owner-confirmed mobile when current ownership and handset evidence are not independently recorded.

workflow.label: Deliver approved owner-confirmed contact
workflow.detail: Only deliver after separately recorded business-public provenance, current owner evidence, handset evidence, and every contact/compliance gate pass.

failures.risk: The NC investor brain route advertises `investors --min 3 --max 8`, but pullNames resolves only `register_source`; the mapping is absent and the job freezes before any name row is read.
failures.mitigation: Add a validated, permitted source adapter and matching `register_source` only if it produces business-public, legally usable records. Otherwise route this industry to a blocked/no-contact state rather than exposing an unusable recipe-B route.

failures.risk: A 3–8 parcel grouping, owner name, owner mailing address, or county file is treated as proof of a commercial investor or as a basis for private-phone discovery.
failures.mitigation: Treat parcel-derived people as out of scope for contact discovery. Require a business-public source and explicit business/operator role before any published-business contact can enter verification.

failures.risk: A published STR/operator or business contact is presented as a current owner-confirmed mobile.
failures.mitigation: Keep published contact, owner role, and handset ownership as independent facts; hold candidate-only records after the contact/compliance gates.

failures.risk: A future source is assumed usable because it is public, despite unclear commercial-use terms or fields.
failures.mitigation: Keep unverified endpoint, field, and permitted-use claims blocked until an authorized free aggregate observation verifies them.

iterations.hypothesis: The configured NC investor route can hand its advertised grouping source to the recipe-B names runner, while other states cleanly fall back when no source is configured.
iterations.test: Five-case code audit on 2026-09-24 using route('real estate investor', state) and registerSourceFor for NC, TX, FL, WA, and PA; no network, source rows, contact fields, or paid calls.
iterations.observed: NC returned recipe B, source `investors --min 3 --max 8`, no fallback, and null registerSource. TX, FL, WA, and PA returned recipe B with fallback A, an empty source list, and null registerSource. Because pullNames freezes when registerSourceFor is null, all five audited cases lack a runnable names-source mapping. This measures routing configuration only, not investor identity, ownership, contact coverage, line type, DNC, or delivery.
iterations.change: Reject the claim that the configured investor grouping is operational. Keep the present route partial and require a source adapter plus a business-public eligibility review before enabling any replacement.

measurement.result: Five state-route fixture cases: NC had recipe B with advertised name source but null registerSource; TX, FL, WA, and PA had recipe B, fallback A, empty sources, and null registerSource. pullNames requires a non-null register source, so this is a configuration/runtime audit only. No live endpoint, person, property, address, phone, or delivery data was collected.

cost.basis: Code audit only; no provider, append, trace, or contact verification was invoked.
cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. The live brain's historical Anas rate has a different denominator and is not a per-clean cost for this review.

implementation.summary: The brain contains a recipe-B investor entry and parcel code, but no register-source mapping or documented investor adapter feeds the names runner. The coded parcel step resolves a person to a home address for a paid trace, which is unsuitable for this review's business-public contact constraint. No permitted business-public investor source is implemented.

nextMeasurement: Before implementation, identify one authorized, free business-public endpoint for active commercial investor/operator records and verify its terms, fields, role semantics, and contact provenance with a 5–20-row aggregate-only sample. Measure business-contact coverage separately from current ownership, handset ownership, mobile line type, DNC/TCPA, reachability, and delivery. Do not use residential parcel or owner data for private-phone discovery.
